tasks.objective: Run Codex through an adapter and an agent-neutral session runner that captures stdout and a 20-line stderr tail silently, with no temporary files.
completion_criteria: A Codex adapter module under src/agents/ exports the AgentAdapter shape from the spec with pure buildArgs and extractFinalMessage; unit tests cover its argument list (with and without model/effort) and its message extraction (non-empty, empty, whitespace-only stdout).

The session runner takes an adapter and launches its executable in the workspace with the prompt on stdin; with the Codex fake fixture writing its final message to stdout, the session yields that message.
The Codex invocation no longer contains --output-last-message and no temp file or directory is created or left behind during a session.
Nothing the agent writes to stdout or stderr reaches the afk process's own stdout or stderr during a session.
A session result exposes at most the last 20 stderr lines in original order, and none when stderr was empty.
Exit code 0 with empty or whitespace-only stdout is a missing response; non-zero exit and launch failure map to the existing execution errors; timeout and abort behavior is unchanged.
afk prints no periodic progress or heartbeat lines while a session is running.
constraints: The adapter has no per-session state, temp files, or cleanup; the session runner owns spawning, stdin, capture, timeout, Ctrl+C and exit mapping.
Existing session tests are updated to the new Codex contract (final message on stdout).

tasks.objective: Provide a registry of built-in adapters and an --agent option that selects the agent for every session of a run, defaulting to Codex.
completion_criteria: A single registry maps agent names to adapters and exposes the default name and the list of supported names.
Without --agent, every session of a run uses the codex adapter; with --agent codex every session including retries uses that adapter.
--agent with an unsupported or empty value yields an option error whose message lists the supported names from the registry, exits 2, and launches no session.
Registering an additional adapter in the registry alone (verified in a test with a stub adapter) makes it accepted by --agent and listed in the error, with no other source change.
--model and --reasoning-effort values are passed to the adapter unchanged, with no agent-specific validation beyond the existing non-empty check; when neither is given no override is supplied.
constraints: Option errors exit 2 (decided with the user); the session-timeout exit code stays 2; input errors (prompt source problems) keep exit 1.
The CLI flag remains --reasoning-effort; only internal naming may become effort.

tasks.objective: Report every run with agent-neutral `[afk]` status lines, including the agent's stderr tail after execution errors.
completion_criteria: Iteration start prints `[afk] Iteration <n>/<max>: starting agent session` to stderr.

Retry, task-failure, execution-error and final status lines carry the `[afk] ` prefix, name no specific agent, and use the wording e.g. `failed to launch agent`, `agent exited unsuccessfully with exit code 3`, `agent exited without a final response`, `agent final response is invalid: <reason>`, `agent session timed out after <n> seconds`; blocked and execution-error finals read `[afk] Run blocked: <text>` and `[afk] Execution error: <detail>`; completion, iteration-limit and interruption finals keep their existing information.
Exit codes are unchanged for completion (0), blocker, execution error and iteration limit (1), timeout (2), and interruption (130/143/129).

After an `[afk] Execution error: …` line (including one that leads to a retry), up to the last 20 stderr lines of that session are printed to stderr in original order; nothing extra is printed when stderr was empty.
No agent stderr is printed after a valid protocol response, a timeout, or an interruption.
A test shows that identical sequences of session results produce identical stderr lines, final status and exit code regardless of which adapter produced them.
constraints: The session prompt, protocol parsing and loop policy are unchanged.

tasks.objective: Support `--agent claude` by running Claude Code in print mode with JSON output and classifying its results per the spec.
completion_criteria: A Claude adapter registered in the registry launches `claude` non-interactively in print mode with JSON output and the auto permission mode, in the workspace, with the prompt on stdin; it adds --model and --effort only when the corresponding afk option is given; it never uses bypassPermissions or any full-access mode.
Exit 0 with a JSON `result` that is a non-empty string is evaluated by the existing protocol parser and acted on exactly as for Codex (repeat, complete, blocked, fail).

Each row of the AC-008 table is covered by a unit test of the adapter and a session-level test with a Claude fake fixture: launch failure; non-zero exit without structured is_error; signal termination; exit 0 with non-JSON stdout (invalid response, parse-failure reason); is_error true on exit 0 or non-zero exit (exited unsuccessfully, reported reason includes the `subtype`); exit 0 with empty stdout or no non-empty `result` string (missing response); protocol violation (invalid response with existing protocol reasons).
The retry-once policy applies to every Claude execution error, and timeout and Ctrl+C end the run with the same messages, no retry, and the same exit codes as for Codex.
constraints: Claude-specific behavior lives only in the adapter module; the run loop and protocol parser stay agent-neutral.
Tests must not require a real Claude installation.

tasks.objective: Run one shared harness behavior test suite against every registered adapter using a per-agent fake executable fixture.
completion_criteria: A shared set of tests covering protocol outcomes, retry policy, iteration limit, timeout, interruption, stderr tail and output wording runs once per registered adapter, iterating the registry.

Each agent has a fake executable fixture that emits its final message the way the real agent does: Codex writes it to stdout (no --output-last-message), Claude writes the JSON result object to stdout.
Adding a fixture for a new registered agent is the only change needed to extend the suite; the suite fails if a registered adapter has no fixture.
`npm test` passes with no real agent installed.
constraints: Per-adapter buildArgs and extractFinalMessage unit tests remain next to each adapter task's tests.

tasks.objective: Make help, README and package metadata describe afk as agent-neutral and document each supported agent.
completion_criteria: --help and -h document `--agent <name>`, list the supported names from the registry, and state the default `codex`; help text refers to "the coding agent" instead of Codex and states that --model and --reasoning-effort values are passed to the agent unchanged.
Help still takes precedence over every other option including an invalid --agent value, exits 0 and starts no session (tested).

README describes afk as agent-neutral, documents --agent, and has a "Supported agents" section giving per agent its prerequisites and how afk launches it: Codex (CLI installed and authenticated with --approve-for-me support); Claude Code (CLI installed and authenticated, auto permission mode available for account and model, `code` skill discoverable e.g. under .claude/skills), plus which harness settings each agent honors.
package.json description no longer names Codex as the only agent, verified by the package test.
constraints: No version bump, changelog or publishing.

tasks.objective: Record manual smoke-check evidence that both adapters work against the real Codex and Claude Code CLIs.
completion_criteria: Evidence records the installed codex and claude CLI versions.
Evidence shows `codex exec --approve-for-me -o <file> -` with piped stdout and a trivial prompt writes the same final message to stdout as to <file>, apart from surrounding whitespace.

Evidence shows `afk --agent codex` and `afk --agent claude`, each run once in a scratch workspace with a prompt naming no specification or task list, ending with `[afk] Run blocked: …` and exit code 1.
Any mismatch with the spec's assumptions (including Claude JSON fields result, is_error, subtype) is listed as a follow-up fix task rather than fixed in this task.
constraints: Manual check, not part of the automated suite; changes no source files.
Requires authenticated Codex and Claude Code installations; if either is unavailable, report that and mark the task not completed.
